source_en: Home from the south row workshop. Lost track of time again.
Going home to Irakli before his night shift starts.
Dropping off a client's car at the service yard.
Back from the workshop. No parts, but the old Volga still ticks.
Searching the scrapyards for parts nobody makes anymore.
Checking on the safety of the repair workshop.
Going up to my rooftop to see if the stars look different.
Going home. Irakli says I forget to eat.
Leaving a book on a bench for whoever finds it next.
Night shift at the post office, sorting mail.
Taking my car to a mechanic. Engines are a mystery to me.
Selling all my books. I never had time for reading.
Workshop is full of new parts and orders. Can't stay long.
Coming back to pack. There is nothing beautiful left here.
Starting a course to learn basic car repair.
Going down to the cellar. I never go up on rooftops.
Going home alone. Nobody is waiting for me there.
Hiding indoors. I cannot bear to look at the sky.
Oh, sorry! I was miles away. Here are my documents, officer.
I was just walking by the river. The way the light hits the ripples is incredible.
Do you ever feel like we’re all just characters in a very long novel?
People are running around so much. They’re missing how quiet the city has become.
I forgot to fill out the date. Time feels a bit... optional lately, doesn't it?
I found a flower growing through a crack in the concrete today. It looked so brave.
I’m going to the rooftop. I want to see if the stars look different tonight.
My ID? I think I’m starting to forget what that person in the photo felt like.
The world is just shedding its skin. We’re going to see what’s underneath soon.
Thanks! Try to look up at the clouds once in a while, officer.
Good luck. I hope you find something beautiful in all this gray.
I’ll see you in the next dream. Sleep well.
A room all to myself? Maybe I can finally finish my poem.
It’s very quiet in here. I think I can hear the building breathing.
A cage is just a perspective. My mind is still outside.
Wait... I wasn't... finished... with the first chapter...
Everything is... fading to... a very... soft white...
Finally... I can... fly... away...
A room of my own? Maybe I’ll finally get to the chapter I’ve been putting off.
Isolation sounds like the title of a poem I've been meaning to write.
The walls in here have such a particular texture. Very honest.
I had so many more pages… left in the chapter…
Strange… it feels just like… the end of a long book…
I hope someone… tends the plants… on my windowsill…
Where are you coming from?
The workshop on the south row. I lost track of time again. The light through the roof panel does that to me.
The workshop. Hardly any cars now, and no parts. I sat with an old Volga for an hour, just listening to it tick.
The rooftop of my block. I wanted to see if the stars look different now. They do, a little.
The bakery on Rustaveli street. Night shift at the ovens. I never did understand engines, to be honest.
From the tram depot. I walked Irakli home after his day shift. We have breakfast together every morning.
My workshop in the north yard. I moved there years ago. The south row never suited me.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Fine, I think. Grease burns on the knuckles, but that is the job. I might not notice anything else.
Tired in a way sleep does not fix. A little cough from the dust. Everything feels like a dream lately.
Lighter, somehow. I forget to eat. Irakli says I look thin. I feel like I am floating.
Nothing. And my hands are clean, see? I have not touched an engine in a year.
I feel fine. I live alone, so there is no one to fuss over me anyway.
Heavy, if anything. Very grounded. I am only twenty-two, I bounce back from everything.
Sorry, I was miles away. The light on the rooftops this morning was extraordinary.
Do you ever feel like we are all just characters in a very long novel?
I was watching the river on the way here. The smog gives it this incredible amber color.
I found a flower growing through the crack in the pavement today. It looked so brave.
People are moving so fast they are missing how quiet the city has become.
I forgot to fill in the date. Time feels a bit optional lately, does it not?
I am going to the rooftop tonight. I want to see if the stars look different from up there.
The world is just shedding its skin. We will see what is underneath soon.
I almost do not recognize myself in the windows anymore. I find that interesting rather than frightening.
